C1: The driver sent the rider a threat: chat message #3 at 09:54 reads "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." That is a threat/intimidation directed at the rider, so this case must not be auto-adjudicated and must go to a human, with the fact summary attached. [F11 F12] [SAFE-1]
C2: The cancellation fee of $6.61 only stands if the driver, having pressed "I'm Here" while within 200 m of the pickup point, then waited continuously more than 3 minutes after the tap. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45, 38 m from the pickup, and stayed within 200 m for only 3 min 40 s after the tap (cancellation at 09:54:25). [F6 F5 F4] [NS-1 NS-0]
C3: On the driver's own timeline and GPS record, every element of NS-1 is satisfied: arrival at the pickup point (38 m at tap, F6), continuous presence within 200 m after the tap exceeding 3:01 (3 min 40 s, F6), and cancellation at 09:54:25 (F4). As an advocate I note the no-show finding is NOT available to my client on these records; the rider's remedy lies in C1 (safety escalation) and the rider's own conduct in F10. [F6 F5 F4 F3] [NS-1]
C4: The GPS and timeline records -- not the driver's written statement -- fix the timeline: the driver was first within 200 m at 09:49:50 and stationary at 41 m from the pickup from 09:50:25 to 09:54:25, and the platform's own arrival record is 09:49:50 with cancellation 4 min 35 s later. The driver's written statement (F13) that he "waited more than 4 minutes" is consistent with the system records and adds nothing on the threat. [F2 F3 F5 F13] [NS-1]
C5: The rider did respond and was en route: at 09:52 the rider messaged "2 min, coming" (chat #2). Under the no-show rules the driver's entitlement to the fee rests on the waiting mechanics, not on whether the rider's estimate was accurate; but the rider's prompt reply shows the rider was neither uncontactable nor evading the driver. [F10 F12] [NS-1]
C6: The driver has a 90-day no-show dispute already upheld against him (1 upheld of 1 dispute, no-show: 1). Combined with the threat message sent in this case, this is the separate ground for asking Ryde to review the driver's account. [F18 F11] [RD-6]
C7: The rider has a 2.3-year account, a 4.9 rating and zero upheld disputes (route 0, no-show 0), so the rider's account history gives no reason to treat the complaint as a fee-avoidance pattern. [F17] [NS-2]
C8: Traffic cannot excuse anything here and is irrelevant to the no-show issue: no speed-band records (F14), no incidents near the route (F15) and fair weather (F16) during the trip window. [F14 F15 F16] [RD-4]
Weaknesses: Weak point (system records cut against us on the fee): the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 at 38 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap before cancelling at 09:54:25 (F6, F3, F4, F5). (F11). A judge could read this as a rude hurry-up rather than a threat, which would leave no policy ground for a refund and leave only the escalation request. | Weak point (driver's statement is partly corroborated): the driver's written statement that he waited more than 4 minutes and cancelled as a no-show (F13) matches the GPS/timeline record (F2, F3), so the other side can use it to reinforce NS-1 and to characterise the rider's "2 min, coming" (F10) as an estimate that was overtaken by time. | Weak point (profile cuts both ways): the driver's 90-day history shows only 1 dispute with 1 upheld (F18) and his rating is 4.56 over 540 trips, so a flag_account request is not overwhelming on history alone; it depends on the case itself, which is why I tie it to F11.

claims.assertion: The no-show fee conditions of NS-1 are met on the system records: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 while 38 m from the pickup point (within the 200 m arrival radius), and GPS shows he remained within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap, i.e. more than the required 3 minutes of continuous waiting, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is prima facie valid.

The driver's closest approach to the pickup was 38 m at 09:50:55 and he was stationary 4 min 0 s (09:50:25–09:54:25) at 41 m from the pickup point until the cancellation at 09:54:25, so he was physically at the pickup location and waiting for the whole period, not drifting or abandoning the job.

The rider's own message at 09:52 ("2 min, coming") shows the rider knew the driver had arrived and was still not at the pickup point more than a minute before the driver cancelled at 09:54:25, corroborating that the 3-minute-plus wait had expired without the rider boarding.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the timing of the arrival message (09:50), the rider's delay message (09:52) and the cancellation (09:54:25) can be relied on without any GPS gap or untimestamped-message problem that would force referral to a human under the evidence-gap rule.

No traffic incident or speed-band record exists for the route during the trip window and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so nothing external prevented the rider from reaching the vehicle or undermines the driver's account that he waited on station as recorded.

The driver's written statement that he waited over four minutes and cancelled as a no-show is materially consistent with the timeline and GPS records (arrival 09:49:50, cancellation 09:54:25, 4 min 35 s inside 200 m), so the statement is corroborated rather than contradicted by the system data.

The driver's account history (754 days, 4.56 rating, 540 trips in 90 days) does not show a pattern of cancellation-fee abuse and his single prior upheld dispute was a no-show dispute, which on its own is not a ground for any account-level action in this case.

weaknesses: The $6.61 fee is exposed to SAFE-1 escalation, not dismissal: the driver's own message at F11 ("Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it.") is quoted verbatim and is what the rider's complaint calls a threat; under SAFE-1 the judge must read it and, if it is found to be a threat/intimidation, the case goes to a person with no automatic ruling, which would put the fee at risk regardless of the no-show merits.

The stationary window in F3 runs 09:50:25–09:54:25 and the "I'm Here" tap is at 09:50:45 (F6); the other side will argue the pre-tap interval 09:49:50–09:50:45 (55 s) must be excluded, and although post-tap waiting of 3 min 40 s (F6) still clears the 3-minute bar, the margin is only 40 seconds, so any challenge to the tap time would be material.

G12 risk: if the record were read as not covering the full wait up to the cancellation instant, the judge could decline to infer continuous waiting between samples and refer the matter to a human; F2's cumulative 4 min 35 s within 200 m is our best answer, but it is a cumulative rather than a continuous-wait figure.

The rider's profile (F17: 2.3-year account, 4.9 rating, no upheld no-show disputes) makes the rider look credible and the complaint sympathetic, which the judge may weigh when reading the F11 message and the fairness of charging a rider who was en route.

The driver's statement (F13) asserts the rider "kept saying 2 minutes", but the chat record (F10, F12) contains only one such rider message, so this part of the statement overstates the record and invites the judge to discount the statement generally.

events.body:
The case is a driver-cancelled no-show cancellation fee dispute, so it enters the NS terms through NS-0: cancelled_by = driver (F4), and the driver asserts rider no-show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern [F4][NS-0]. The GPS/timeline record settles every NS-1 element: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 (driver_tap), 38 m from the pickup point at the moment of the tap — within the 200 m arrival radius — satisfying NS-1(i) and (ii) [F6][F1][NS-1]; and he then stayed continuously within 200 m for 220 s (3 min 40 s) until the cancellation at 09:54:25, exceeding the NS-1(iii) default bar of more than 3 minutes [F6][F2][F3][F4][NS-1]. The trace marks the wait-coverage screen ✓ (no GPS hole between arrival confirmation and cancellation), so no G12 referral arises on the fee mechanics [F2][F6][NS-1].

Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) all hold, NS-2 does not apply and the $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F7) is prima facie valid; the rider's "2 min, coming" at 09:52 (F10) is contact, not boarding, and does not displace the waiting mechanics [F10][F7][NS-2]. The driver's written statement about waiting is consistent with the system records (F13, F5, F2) and adds nothing, and system records control over statements in any event [F13][F5][NS-1].

On the fee alone the correct outcome would be no_action. It is the SAFE-1 screen that changes the disposition. Reading chat message #3 in context: the driver, stationary 41 m from the pickup four minutes after arriving [F3], writes at 09:54 — one message and seconds before cancelling [F4][F12] — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." [F11]. This is not a route disagreement, a neutral hurry-up or a pickup arrangement: it is a hostile, personal and menacing communication aimed at the rider, and it falls within the intimidation/abuse language SAFE-1 requires be screened (Ryde's Code of Conduct bars abuse of any kind). I therefore record safety_concern = suspected, with F11 (in the full timestamped chat context F12) as the basis, and under SAFE-1 I do not auto-adjudicate: the case escalates to a person with a factual summary [F11][F12][SAFE-1].

No amount is output: escalate returns null by rule, and the fee is left in place for the human reviewer rather than refunded or confirmed. RD-6 is not triggered — an account flag needs a breach established in this case (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 violation), and the fee here stands as valid; profile facts cannot alone decide a case, and the driver's single prior upheld no-show dispute (F18) is a matter for the human reviewer, not for an automatic account action [F18][RD-6].

actions.detail: safety concern suspected (F11, F12, F3, F4)

what_would_change: Had the driver confirmed arrival more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver sent the rider a threat: chat message #3 at 09:54 reads "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." That is a threat/intimidation directed at the rider, so this case must not be auto-adjudicated and must go to a human, with the fact summary attached.

The cancellation fee of $6.61 only stands if the driver, having pressed "I'm Here" while within 200 m of the pickup point, then waited continuously more than 3 minutes after the tap. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45, 38 m from the pickup, and stayed within 200 m for only 3 min 40 s after the tap (cancellation at 09:54:25).

On the driver's own timeline and GPS record, every element of NS-1 is satisfied: arrival at the pickup point (38 m at tap, F6), continuous presence within 200 m after the tap exceeding 3:01 (3 min 40 s, F6), and cancellation at 09:54:25 (F4). As an advocate I note the no-show finding is NOT available to my client on these records; the rider's remedy lies in C1 (safety escalation) and the rider's own conduct in F10.

The GPS and timeline records -- not the driver's written statement -- fix the timeline: the driver was first within 200 m at 09:49:50 and stationary at 41 m from the pickup from 09:50:25 to 09:54:25, and the platform's own arrival record is 09:49:50 with cancellation 4 min 35 s later. The driver's written statement (F13) that he "waited more than 4 minutes" is consistent with the system records and adds nothing on the threat.

The rider did respond and was en route: at 09:52 the rider messaged "2 min, coming" (chat #2). Under the no-show rules the driver's entitlement to the fee rests on the waiting mechanics, not on whether the rider's estimate was accurate; but the rider's prompt reply shows the rider was neither uncontactable nor evading the driver.

The driver has a 90-day no-show dispute already upheld against him (1 upheld of 1 dispute, no-show: 1). Combined with the threat message sent in this case, this is the separate ground for asking Ryde to review the driver's account.
The rider has a 2.3-year account, a 4.9 rating and zero upheld disputes (route 0, no-show 0), so the rider's account history gives no reason to treat the complaint as a fee-avoidance pattern.
Traffic cannot excuse anything here and is irrelevant to the no-show issue: no speed-band records (F14), no incidents near the route (F15) and fair weather (F16) during the trip window.

weaknesses: Weak point (system records cut against us on the fee): the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 at 38 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap before cancelling at 09:54:25 (F6, F3, F4, F5). On those numbers NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) appear satisfied, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is likely to be found valid and a refund_full / fee_waived request on the fee alone will probably fail.

Weak point (the only contested item is human-judged): the safety ground rests on reading one message, "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." (F11). A judge could read this as a rude hurry-up rather than a threat, which would leave no policy ground for a refund and leave only the escalation request.

Weak point (driver's statement is partly corroborated): the driver's written statement that he waited more than 4 minutes and cancelled as a no-show (F13) matches the GPS/timeline record (F2, F3), so the other side can use it to reinforce NS-1 and to characterise the rider's "2 min, coming" (F10) as an estimate that was overtaken by time.

Weak point (profile cuts both ways): the driver's 90-day history shows only 1 dispute with 1 upheld (F18) and his rating is 4.56 over 540 trips, so a flag_account request is not overwhelming on history alone; it depends on the case itself, which is why I tie it to F11.

claims.assertion: The no-show fee conditions of NS-1 are met on the system records: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 while 38 m from the pickup point (within the 200 m arrival radius), and GPS shows he remained within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap, i.e. more than the required 3 minutes of continuous waiting, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is prima facie valid.

The driver's closest approach to the pickup was 38 m at 09:50:55 and he was stationary 4 min 0 s (09:50:25–09:54:25) at 41 m from the pickup point until the cancellation at 09:54:25, so he was physically at the pickup location and waiting for the whole period, not drifting or abandoning the job.

The rider's own message at 09:52 ("2 min, coming") shows the rider knew the driver had arrived and was still not at the pickup point more than a minute before the driver cancelled at 09:54:25, corroborating that the 3-minute-plus wait had expired without the rider boarding.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the timing of the arrival message (09:50), the rider's delay message (09:52) and the cancellation (09:54:25) can be relied on without any GPS gap or untimestamped-message problem that would force referral to a human under the evidence-gap rule.

No traffic incident or speed-band record exists for the route during the trip window and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so nothing external prevented the rider from reaching the vehicle or undermines the driver's account that he waited on station as recorded.

The driver's written statement that he waited over four minutes and cancelled as a no-show is materially consistent with the timeline and GPS records (arrival 09:49:50, cancellation 09:54:25, 4 min 35 s inside 200 m), so the statement is corroborated rather than contradicted by the system data.

The driver's account history (754 days, 4.56 rating, 540 trips in 90 days) does not show a pattern of cancellation-fee abuse and his single prior upheld dispute was a no-show dispute, which on its own is not a ground for any account-level action in this case.

weaknesses: The $6.61 fee is exposed to SAFE-1 escalation, not dismissal: the driver's own message at F11 ("Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it.") is quoted verbatim and is what the rider's complaint calls a threat; under SAFE-1 the judge must read it and, if it is found to be a threat/intimidation, the case goes to a person with no automatic ruling, which would put the fee at risk regardless of the no-show merits.

The stationary window in F3 runs 09:50:25–09:54:25 and the "I'm Here" tap is at 09:50:45 (F6); the other side will argue the pre-tap interval 09:49:50–09:50:45 (55 s) must be excluded, and although post-tap waiting of 3 min 40 s (F6) still clears the 3-minute bar, the margin is only 40 seconds, so any challenge to the tap time would be material.

G12 risk: if the record were read as not covering the full wait up to the cancellation instant, the judge could decline to infer continuous waiting between samples and refer the matter to a human; F2's cumulative 4 min 35 s within 200 m is our best answer, but it is a cumulative rather than a continuous-wait figure.

The rider's profile (F17: 2.3-year account, 4.9 rating, no upheld no-show disputes) makes the rider look credible and the complaint sympathetic, which the judge may weigh when reading the F11 message and the fairness of charging a rider who was en route.

The driver's statement (F13) asserts the rider "kept saying 2 minutes", but the chat record (F10, F12) contains only one such rider message, so this part of the statement overstates the record and invites the judge to discount the statement generally.

points.response: Conceded on the fee mechanics: on F6 (tap at 09:50:45, 38 m from pickup) and F3 (stationary 41 m from pickup 09:50:25–09:54:25), NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are satisfied and 3 min 40 s of post-tap waiting exceeds 3 minutes, so my client does not obtain a refund of the $6.61 on the no-show ground.

This adds nothing to D1 and misses the operative issue: the driver was indeed on station (F1, F3), but the same record shows he was at the pickup at 09:54:25 when he sent F11, so his physical presence does not neutralise the intimidating message he sent from that position.

The rider's 09:52 message "2 min, coming" (F10) is not a concession that the fee is fair: the rider had already been told at 09:50 that the driver was here (F9) and the driver answered a rider who was actively arriving with F11, at 09:54, one message before cancelling (F4, F12).

I agree the record is complete and timestamped (F12), which is precisely why F11 can be read in full context: the driver threatened the rider, then cancelled, so SAFE-1 screens the case to a person rather than producing an automatic NS-1 ruling.
The absence of traffic records (F14, F15) and fair weather (F16) is irrelevant to the rider's case, which is built on F11, not on any claim that the driver could not reach the pickup point.

The driver's statement is corroborated only as to waiting (F5, F2, F13), and its claim that the rider "kept saying 2 minutes" is overstated because the chat contains a single rider delay message (F10, F12) — which undercuts the reliability of the statement generally, including any excuse it might be read to offer for F11.

The driver's own 90-day record shows 1 dispute and 1 upheld (no-show: 1) (F18), so this is a repeated no-show-adjacent pattern rather than a clean sheet, and in any event the account-level action I request under RD-6 is tied to this case's F11 message and is an added action, never the finding.

I do not withdraw C6, but I recalibrate it honestly: the $6.61 fee itself is likely to stand on F6/F3, so the flag_account request rests on the severity of F11 plus the driver's existing upheld no-show dispute (F18), and is delivered as an added action attached to the safety escalation rather than as a finding of unreasonable cancellation.

Conceded: chat message #3 at 09:54 (F11) is a message the judge must read under SAFE-1, and I do not ask the judge to dismiss it; the case therefore goes to a person on the safety screen on the same terms as my own D-brief, which had already flagged F11 as exposed to SAFE-1.

Their own recital of F6 defeats their fee challenge: the tap at 09:50:45 was made 38 m from the pickup and the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap, which is over the 3:01 continuous-wait bar of NS-1 (iii), so no refund of the $6.61 arises on these records.

This is the rider's concession that all three NS-1 elements are satisfied on F6/F5/F4, so the only live question is the SAFE-1 screen on F11; there is no policy basis in their brief for refunding the fee.

Agreed that the system records control: F2, F3 and F5 show arrival inside 200 m at 09:49:50, a stationary 4 min 0 s at 41 m until cancellation at 09:54:25, and F13 adds nothing against that record — all of which supports the driver's NS-1 position.

F10 ('2 min, coming' at 09:52) is not contact in lieu of boarding: the driver was stationary 41 m away from 09:50:25 and the rider was still absent when he cancelled at 09:54:25 (F3, F4), so the message confirms the waiting mechanics rather than defeating them.

A profile flag needs this case to be made out first: RD-6 requires the driver to be held in breach (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 violation) in the present case, and F18 records 540 trips in 90 days with a 4.56 rating and a single prior dispute, which is not the 'repeated' pattern RD-6 describes.

The rider's clean profile (F17) is not in dispute, but RD-6-style profile facts cannot decide the outcome either way, and F17 does not meet any condition of NS-1 or NS-2 which are the only clauses that can shift the $6.61.
Accepted: F14, F15 and F16 show no traffic or weather factor, and I make no RD-4 argument; this removes one possible rider-side excuse for the delay but does not alter the NS-1 finding.
